# Node SDK for CloudEvents [![Build Status](https://travis-ci.com/grant/cloudevents.svg?branch=master)](https://travis-ci.com/grant/cloudevents) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/cloudevents.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cloudevents)

An SDK providing primitives for working with Cloud Events.
Supports the [CE SDK Spec](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/master/SDK.md).
Includes TypeScript support.
Only supports major versions

## Quickstart

Install the package:

```sh
npm i cloudevents
```

Create new CloudEvents:

```js
import { CloudEvent } from 'cloudevents';

const event = CloudEvent.newEvent({
  id: 'ABC-123',
  type: 'com.cloudevents.readme.sent',
  source: 'http://localhost:8080/',
  specversion: '1.0',
  data: {},
});
```

Sending a CloudEvent via the HTTP Transport with Binary v0.2 encoding:

```js
const transport = CloudEvent.newHTTPTransport({
  target: 'http://localhost:8080/',
  encoding: CloudEvent.HTTPBinaryV1,
});

const client = CloudEvent.newClient({ transport });
client.send(event);
```

Or, the transport can be set to produce CloudEvents using the selected encoding
but not change the provided event version, here the client is set to output structured encoding:

```js
const transport = CloudEvent.newHTTPTransport({
  target: 'http://localhost:8080/',
  encoding: CloudEvent.StructuredEncoding,
});
```

If you are using advanced transport features or have implemented your own transport integration,
provide it to a client so your integration does not change:

```js
const transport = CloudEvent.newHTTPTransport({
  port: 8080,
  path: '/events/'
});
const client = CloudEvent.newClient(transport, {});
```

Check out the [`docs/`](docs/README.md) sample sender and receiver applications for working demo.
